description: Checking designs in EAGLE 9.6: the board's Design Rules (Design Rules dialog with its File, Layers, Clearance, Distance, Sizes, Annular Ring, Shapes, Supply, Masks and Misc tabs, the .dru parameters behind them and the layer-setup syntax for blind, buried and micro vias), Live DRC, DRC error types, the ERRORS dialog, the Electrical Rule Check with its messages and consistency errors, pin directions, ULP access to errors, the autorouter's use of the rules, cross-reference labels, and the design-rule files shipped with the installation.

tools.name: Design Rules
tools.description: The set of manufacturing parameters a board must satisfy, checked by the Design Rule Check (DRC) and also obeyed by the autorouter and interactive routing. The rules are stored inside the board file, so a board sent to a manufacturer carries them; .dru files are only for copying rule sets between boards. New boards take their rules from default.dru in the first directory of Options > Directories > Design rules, or from built-in defaults if none exists.
tools.usage: Board editor > Edit > Design Rules... | DRC (dialog) | DRC LOAD file.dru;
tools.example: Load the board house's rule file before routing: DRC LOAD eC_2Layer_PClass6_BaseCopperO18_eCDefault.dru; then route and finally run DRC;
tools.notes: Clearance and distance values are limited by the internal resolution of 1/320000 mm. Net classes can raise width, drill and clearance values for individual signals.

tools.name: Design Rules dialog
tools.description: Opened by DRC without a terminating ';' (or Edit > Design Rules...), it holds the rule tabs File, Layers, Clearance, Distance, Sizes, Annular Ring, Shapes, Supply, Masks and Misc, each parameter illustrated by a small picture. Apply stores the values in the board (annular ring and shape changes show immediately), Check stores them and runs the DRC over the whole board, and Select lets you drag a rectangle so that only errors at least partly inside it are reported.
tools.usage: DRC   (dialog) | DRC;   (check immediately) | DRC (x1 y1) (x2 y2);   (check an area) | DRC *   (edit rules without checking)
tools.example:
DRC *          # adjust rules only
DRC;           # full check with the stored rules
DRC (0 0) (40 30);   # check only the lower-left 40 x 30 area
tools.notes: All signal layers and airwires are checked whether visible or not. Electrically irrelevant objects (wires in footprints, rectangles, circles, texts) are not checked against each other for clearance. Rule changes are part of UNDO/REDO.

tools.name: Live DRC
tools.description: Since 8.4 the design rules can be checked continuously while editing and routing, so violations appear immediately instead of after a DRC run. It is switched with the Live DRC checkbox in the Set dialog or the SET command, and the fill style of DRC error polygons is set with SET DRC_FILL (default LtSlash).
tools.usage: SET LIVE_DRC ON | OFF;   SET DRC_FILL fill_name;
tools.example:
SET LIVE_DRC ON;
SET DRC_FILL XHatch;
tools.notes: Live DRC costs performance on large boards (several releases improved MOVE performance with live DRC); switch it off for bulk edits and run DRC; at the end.

tools.name: Design Rules > File
tools.description: Shows the description of the current rule set, which can be edited (HTML allowed) with Edit Description and should be changed whenever you define your own rules. Load... reads a .dru file into the board and Save as... writes the board's rules to a .dru file; the dialog title gets a trailing '*' while the rules differ from the loaded or saved file.
tools.usage: Design Rules dialog > File > Load... | Save as... | Edit Description   (command line: DRC LOAD|SAVE|MERGE file;)
tools.example:
DRC SAVE D:/Company/dru/company_2layer_6mil.dru;
DRC MERGE D:/Company/dru/masks_only.dru;   # merge some parameters, keep the others
tools.notes: Dragging a .dru from the Control Panel onto a board editor, or its context menu entry 'Load into Board', does the same as Load.

tools.name: Design Rules > Layers (Setup)
tools.description: Defines which signal layers exist and which vias are possible with a setup string of layer numbers joined by '*' (core material) or '+' (prepreg/other isolation); parentheses (...) enclose layers that through vias connect, and [t:...:b] marks blind vias that reach from the top down to layer t or from the bottom up to layer b. The default (1*16) is a two-layer board with vias through the whole board; only layers in the setup are available to DISPLAY, LAYER, LINE and ROUTE.

parameters.description: Core between the two layers (FR4 or similar).
Prepreg or other isolation between the layers.
Through/buried vias through the enclosed stack.

parameters.name: [t: ... :b]
parameters.description: Blind vias from the top to layer t and/or from the bottom to layer b; one side may be omitted.

tools.example:
16                         # single-sided board, no vias
(1*2+15*16)                # 4 layers, vias through all layers
(1*2+3*14+15*16)           # 6 layers, vias through all layers
((1*2)+(15*16))            # 4 layers: buried pairs 1-2 and 15-16 plus through vias
[2:1+((2*3)+(14*15))+16:15]  # 6 layers with blind vias 1-2 and 16-15
tools.notes: The core/prepreg sequence only changes the colours of the stack picture; the real build-up must be agreed with the manufacturer. A blind via from layer a to b also allows blind vias to every layer between them. Pads are always allowed even if no 1-16 via exists in the setup.

tools.name: Layer setup examples (blind, buried and micro vias)
tools.description: The layer-setup_designrules document shipped with EAGLE illustrates typical stacks with their setup strings. It covers prepreg/core/prepreg builds with blind or micro vias on the outer layers, core-prepreg-core builds with buried vias, multiple prepreg layers with nested blind vias, and 12- to 16-layer HDI stacks with stacked blind vias.
tools.usage: Copy the matching string into Design Rules > Layers > Setup
tools.notes: Blind-via aspect ratio and micro-via size limits are set on the Sizes tab; via lengths used on the board decide how many drill files the CAM Processor writes.

tools.name: Design Rules > Layers (copper and isolation thickness)
tools.description: Besides the setup string, the Layers tab stores the copper thickness of every signal layer and the isolation thickness between them. These values mainly matter for boards with blind or micro vias, where the via depth relative to the drill diameter is checked against the blind-via ratio.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Layers > Copper / Isolation   (.dru keys mtCopper = 16 values, mtIsolate = 15 values)
tools.notes: A Blind Via Ratio error is fixed either by a larger via drill (Sizes tab) or thinner layers (Layers tab).

tools.name: Design Rules > Clearance
tools.description: Minimum clearances between copper objects in signal layers: wires, pads, vias and SMDs of different signals, plus same-signal checks between SMDs, pads and vias (0 disables a same-signal check). These are absolute process limits to be taken from the board house; the effective clearance between two signals is the larger of this value and their net classes' clearance.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Clearance   (.dru keys mdWireWire, mdWirePad, mdWireVia, mdPadPad, mdPadVia, mdViaVia, mdSmdPad, mdSmdVia, mdSmdSmd, mdViaViaSameLayer)
tools.example:
mdWireWire = 6mil
mdWirePad = 6mil
mdWireVia = 6mil
mdPadPad = 6mil
mdPadVia = 6mil
mdViaVia = 6mil
mdSmdPad = 6mil
mdSmdVia = 6mil
mdSmdSmd = 6mil
tools.notes: Polygons of the same rank and polygons in footprints additionally keep their Isolate distance. Micro vias are checked like wires. The _OUTLINES_ polygon ignores these values. The plausibility check requires same-signal values not larger than different-signal values.

tools.name: Design Rules > Distance
tools.description: Minimum distance between copper and the board dimension (objects in layer 20 and holes) and between any two drill holes. Only signals connected to at least one pad or SMD are checked against the dimension, so edge markers in copper do not cause errors.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Distance > Copper/Dimension, Drill/Hole   (.dru keys mdCopperDimension, mdDrill)
tools.example:
mdCopperDimension = 40mil
mdDrill = 6mil
tools.notes: Copper/Dimension = 0 (compatibility with 3.5x) disables the check and makes polygons ignore the Dimension layer except holes, and the DRC then does not detect holes placed on tracks.

tools.name: Design Rules > Sizes
tools.description: Minimum width of any object in signal layers and minimum drill diameter, both process limits from the board house (net classes may demand larger values). It also defines the minimum micro-via drill - vias with a drill between this value and Minimum Drill count as micro vias, and a value above Minimum Drill (default) means none are used - and the minimum blind-via ratio of drill diameter to via depth.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Sizes > Minimum Width, Minimum Drill, Min. Micro Via, Min. Blind Via Ratio   (.dru keys msWidth, msDrill, msMicroVia, msBlindViaRatio)
tools.example:
msWidth = 6mil
msDrill = 0.35mm
msMicroVia = 9.99mm       # no micro vias
msBlindViaRatio = 0.500000   # board house ratio 1:0.5
tools.notes: Violations are reported as Width, Drill Size, Micro Via Size and Blind Via Ratio errors. Text in signal layers is checked for width too.

tools.name: Design Rules > Annular Ring (pads)
tools.description: Sets the copper ring left around a pad's hole as a percentage of the drill diameter, clamped by an absolute minimum and maximum, separately for top, inner and bottom layers. If the library diameter of a pad gives a larger ring, that is used in the outer layers; a library pad diameter of 0 lets the ring come entirely from these rules.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Annular Ring > Pads Top / Inner / Bottom   (.dru keys rvPadTop, rvPadInner, rvPadBottom, rlMinPadTop, rlMaxPadTop, rlMinPadInner, rlMaxPadInner, rlMinPadBottom, rlMaxPadBottom)
tools.example:
rvPadTop = 0.250000     # 25 % of the drill
rlMinPadTop = 10mil
rlMaxPadTop = 20mil   # 40 mil drill -> 10 mil ring; 24 mil drill -> clamped to 10 mil
tools.notes: Set min = max for a fixed ring width (the percentage then has no effect). Pads in inner layers are always round. Older versions called this tab Restring.

tools.name: Design Rules > Annular Ring (vias and micro vias)
tools.description: The same percentage-with-limits rule for vias (outer and inner layers) and micro vias (outer and inner). The resulting diameters can be seen with INFO on a via, which reports the predefined diameter and the calculated outer and inner diameters.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Annular Ring > Vias Outer/Inner, Micro Vias Outer/Inner   (.dru keys rvViaOuter, rvViaInner, rlMinViaOuter, rlMaxViaOuter, rlMinViaInner, rlMaxViaInner, rvMicroViaOuter, rvMicroViaInner, rlMinMicroViaOuter, rlMaxMicroViaOuter, rlMinMicroViaInner, rlMaxMicroViaInner)
tools.example:
rvViaOuter = 0.250000
rlMinViaOuter = 8mil
rlMaxViaOuter = 20mil
rlMinMicroViaOuter = 4mil
tools.notes: To judge the real pad/via size per layer, set the colour of layers 17 Pads and 18 Vias to the background colour so that the signal-layer shapes are shown.

tools.name: Design Rules > Annular Ring (Diameter option)
tools.description: Controls whether a diameter defined for a pad in the library or for a via in the board is also applied in the inner layers. Enable it if the predefined diameter exceeds the calculated one and pads/vias should have the same size in all layers; new boards have it off, boards converted from 3.5 or older have it on.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Annular Ring > Diameter checkboxes   (.dru key useDiameter)
tools.example: useDiameter = 13     # value stored in the shipped default.dru

tools.name: Design Rules > Shapes (SMD roundness)
tools.description: Makes rectangular SMD pads rounder for the whole board: 0 % keeps sharp corners and 100 % gives maximum rounding (a square SMD becomes round). The roundness can be limited by an absolute minimum and maximum.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Shapes > Smds Roundness   (.dru keys srRoundness, srMinRoundness, srMaxRoundness)
tools.example:
srRoundness = 0.250000   # 25 % rounded SMD corners
srMinRoundness = 0mil
srMaxRoundness = 0mil

tools.name: Design Rules > Shapes (pads)
tools.description: Overrides the pad shape of the library for top and bottom separately (as in library, square, round or octagon) and gives pads marked 'first' in the library a special shape. Elongation sets the length-to-width ratio of Long and Offset pads in percent: 0 % is 1:1, 100 % is 2:1 (default) and the maximum 200 % is 4:1.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Shapes > Pads Top / Bottom / First, Elongation Long / Offset   (.dru keys psTop, psBottom, psFirst, psElongationLong, psElongationOffset)
tools.example:
psTop = -1          # -1 = As in library (default)
psBottom = -1
psFirst = -1
psElongationLong = 100
psElongationOffset = 100
tools.notes: Pads and vias in inner layers are always round, sized by the annular ring rules.

tools.name: Design Rules > Supply
tools.description: Parameters for thermal connections between pads/vias and copper polygons of the same signal: the thermal isolation (gap between the polygon and the pad's annular ring) and whether vias get thermals as well (otherwise they are connected solidly). The width of the thermal bridges follows the polygon's line width.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Supply > Thermal isolation, Generate thermals for vias   (.dru keys slThermalIsolate, slThermalsForVias)
tools.example:
slThermalIsolate = 10mil
slThermalsForVias = 0
tools.notes: Individual polygons can drop thermals with CHANGE THERMALS OFF, and pads/SMDs flagged NOTHERMALS in the library are always connected fully. The older keys slThermalGap, slMinThermalGap, slMaxThermalGap, slAnnulusIsolate, slAnnulusRestring and slThermalRestring still appear in the shipped default.dru.

tools.name: Design Rules > Masks (solder stop)
tools.description: Solder stop mask openings are generated in tStop/bStop for SMDs, pads and vias whose drill exceeds the Limit value, enlarged by a percentage of the smaller pad dimension clamped between minimum and maximum. The default is a fixed 4 mil oversize (min = max, so the percentage has no effect) and Limit 0, i.e. every via gets an opening.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Masks > Stop, Limit   (.dru keys mvStopFrame, mlMinStopFrame, mlMaxStopFrame, mlViaStopLimit)
tools.example:
mvStopFrame = 1.000000
mlMinStopFrame = 4mil
mlMaxStopFrame = 4mil
mlViaStopLimit = 24mil    # vias up to 24 mil drill are covered (tented)
tools.notes: A covered via can still get an opening with CHANGE STOP ON; pads/SMDs with STOP off in the library get none.

tools.name: Design Rules > Masks (cream)
tools.description: Solder cream (paste) openings are generated in tCream/bCream for SMDs only. The Cream value is entered as a positive number but reduces the opening relative to the SMD, as a percentage of its smaller dimension with minimum and maximum limits; the default 0 makes the opening equal to the SMD.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Masks > Cream   (.dru keys mvCreamFrame, mlMinCreamFrame, mlMaxCreamFrame)
tools.example:
mvCreamFrame = 0.100000
mlMinCreamFrame = 0mil
mlMaxCreamFrame = 2mil    # shrink paste openings by 10 %, at most 2 mil
tools.notes: SMDs with CREAM off in the library get no paste opening; the CAM Processor suppresses paste of unpopulated parts of the current assembly variant.

tools.name: Design Rules > Misc (checks)
tools.description: Switches optional DRC checks: Check grid (objects off the current grid), Check angle (tracks not at multiples of 45 degrees), Check font (texts in signal layers not in vector font, default on) and Check restrict (copper in tRestrict/bRestrict areas, default on), plus the stop mask check. The former 'Stop after ... errors' limit was removed; maxErrors in .dru files is ignored.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Misc   (.dru keys checkGrid, checkAngle, checkFont, checkRestrict, checkStop, maxErrors)
tools.example:
checkGrid = 0
checkAngle = 0
checkFont = 1
checkRestrict = 1
checkStop = 0
tools.notes: Boards saved by 9.x also store checkValues, checkNames, checkWireStubs and checkPolygonWidth; related release-note features are the option to omit tValues/bValues from the DRC (8.5) and ignoring wire stubs absorbed by polygons (9.2). Restricted areas made of cutout polygons and copper/restrict objects inside the same footprint are not checked.

tools.name: Design Rules > Misc (differential pairs)
tools.description: Two parameters for differential pairs (signals named xxx_P / xxx_N in the same net class). Max. length difference defines the tolerance for which MEANDER shows the length deviation in green instead of red (default 10 mm), and the Gap factor (1 to 20, default 2.5) sets the spacing between the loops of meanders in differential pairs.
tools.usage: Design Rules > Misc > Max. length difference in differential pairs, Gap factor   (.dru keys dpMaxLengthDifference, dpGapFactor)
tools.example:
dpMaxLengthDifference = 10mm
dpGapFactor = 2.5
tools.notes: Pair spacing, wire width and via size come from the pair's net class, not from these rules.

tools.name: Net classes and design rules
tools.description: Net classes (CLASS command) give groups of signals their own minimum wire width, via drill and clearances to other classes. The DRC always uses the larger of the design-rule value and the class value, so if an error persists after relaxing the rules, check the net class of the reported object.
tools.usage: CLASS number [name [width [clearance [drill]]]] [number:clearance ..]   (dialog without parameters; stored as <class> elements)
tools.example:
CLASS 1 power 0.4mm 0.2mm 0.6mm;
CHANGE CLASS power    # then click the VCC and GND signals
tools.notes: Routing tools pick width and drill from the class when Options > Set > Misc > Auto set route width and drill is on.

tools.name: DRC error: Clearance / Overlap
tools.description: Clearance reports copper objects closer than allowed by the Clearance tab or the net class (whichever is larger), including polygon Isolate values for same-rank polygons and polygons in footprints; Overlap reports copper of different signals that actually touch. The error polygon's size shows how far the limit is exceeded.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC; browse with ERRORS
tools.example: Clearance on layer 1 between wire (GND) and pad U1.4 -> move the wire or reduce the class clearance if the manufacturer allows it.
tools.notes: Set the same-signal clearance to 0 to suppress same-signal checks. Since 7.5 there is also a special DRC error for intersecting signal polygons with the same rank.

tools.name: DRC error: Width / Drill Size / Micro Via Size / Blind Via Ratio
tools.description: Size-related errors: Width (copper or vector-text line thinner than Minimum Width or the class width), Drill Size (pad, via or hole drill below Minimum Drill or the class drill for vias), Micro Via Size (micro-via drill below Min. Micro Via) and Blind Via Ratio (via depth too large for its drill diameter).
tools.usage: Reported by DRC; limits on the Sizes tab and in CLASS
tools.example: Blind Via Ratio at via (12.7 8.3): enlarge the via drill (CHANGE DRILL) or reduce the layer thickness in the Layers tab.

tools.name: DRC error: Dimension / Drill Distance
tools.description: Dimension reports SMDs, pads and connected copper closer to a Dimension-layer line (board outline) than the Copper/Dimension value. Drill Distance reports holes closer to each other than the Drill/Hole value of the Distance tab.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC; limits on the Distance tab
tools.example: Dimension error at pad J1.1, which lies 0.2 mm from the outline while Copper/Dimension is 0.25 mm -> move the connector inward or agree a smaller edge distance with the fabricator.
tools.notes: With Copper/Dimension = 0 the Dimension check is off and holes on tracks go undetected.

tools.name: DRC error: Airwire
tools.description: Since 8.1.1 unrouted connections are listed as errors under their own Airwires heading. Only a board without airwires is guaranteed to have all connections made.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC
tools.example: Airwires: 2 -> RATSNEST; to recalculate, then ROUTE the remaining connections or check whether a polygon should connect them.

tools.name: DRC error: Stop Mask
tools.description: Reported when silkscreen objects (tPlace/tNames/tValues for top parts, bPlace/bNames/bValues for bottom parts) overlap solder stop openings in tStop/bStop, which would put ink on solderable copper. The check needs the corresponding layers to be displayed and always assumes the vector font.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC when the stop mask check is enabled and the layers are displayed
tools.example: Stop Mask on layer 21 at R5: SMASH R5 and move its name text off the pads.

tools.name: DRC error: No Vector Font / No real vector font
tools.description: With Check font enabled, texts in signal layers must use EAGLE's vector font because the CAM Processor renders only that font. 'No real vector font' flags texts that only look like vector font on screen because 'Always vector font' is active in Options > User interface.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC (Misc > Check font)
tools.example: CHANGE FONT VECTOR   # then click the offending copper text; or set Always vector font + Persistent in this drawing

tools.name: DRC error: Restrict / Keepout
tools.description: Restrict reports top/bottom wires or vias inside restricted areas drawn in tRestrict/bRestrict (and vRestrict for vias). Keepout reports overlapping component keepout areas in tKeepout/bKeepout; this check runs only when those layers are displayed and the keepouts are defined in the footprints.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC (Misc > Check restrict for Restrict)
tools.example: DISPLAY 39 40; DRC;   # include keepout checking
tools.notes: Restricted areas and copper defined in the same footprint are not checked against each other.

tools.name: DRC error: Layer Abuse / Layer Setup
tools.description: Layer Abuse means that objects were drawn manually in layers 17 Pads or 18 Vias, which are reserved for automatically generated pads and vias. Layer Setup means an object lies in a signal layer not defined by the layer setup, or a via has a length the setup does not allow (e.g. an illegal blind/buried span); supply layers missing from the setup are reported the same way.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC
tools.example: Layer Setup on layer 2 with setup (1*16): change the setup to (1*2+15*16) or move the objects to layer 1/16.

tools.name: DRC error: Off Grid / Angle / Wire Style
tools.description: Optional and style checks: Off Grid (object not on the current grid, Misc > Check grid) and Angle (track not at 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees, Misc > Check angle) are both off by default. Wire Style is reported when a routed signal wire uses a LongDash, ShortDash or DashDot style, which the DRC treats like a continuous line.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC
tools.example: Wire Style on signal CLK: CHANGE STYLE CONTINUOUS and click the wire.

tools.name: DRC error: Invalid Polygon
tools.description: The polygon outline overlaps or crosses itself, so its fill cannot be calculated correctly. RATSNEST reports the same problem; fix the contour in the board or, for polygons in footprints, in the library.
tools.usage: Reported by DRC and RATSNEST
tools.example: SHOW the polygon, MOVE its crossing vertex, then RATSNEST; DRC;

tools.name: ERRORS dialog
tools.description: Lists the results of ERC or DRC in up to four branches: Consistency errors, Errors, Warnings and Approved. Selecting an entry marks it in the drawing (double click or 'Centered' centres the view); Processed greys out a fixed entry until the next check, Approve moves an acceptable message to Approved (stored in the drawing file as documentation) and Disapprove moves it back, Clear all empties all but the approved list.
tools.usage: ERRORS   (dialog; runs ERC/DRC first if none was run) | ERRORS CLEAR;
tools.example: ERRORS > select Errors > Approve all (after review) > save the board, so the approvals are documented in the file.
tools.notes: Consistency errors cannot be approved. Error polygons are shown only in the editor, never printed or sent to the CAM Processor, and cannot be deleted with DELETE; the list shows only errors in displayed layers and can be sorted by type or layer/sheet.

tools.name: Electrical Rule Check (ERC)
tools.description: Checks a schematic for electrical mistakes such as open or conflicting pins, and lists the findings as errors and warnings in the ERRORS dialog. If the board is loaded, it also cross-checks schematic and board and switches forward & back annotation on or off accordingly; it detects mismatches between implicit power/supply pins and the board's signals.
tools.usage: ERC   (schematic editor; Tools > Erc...)
tools.example: ERC;   # then ERRORS to review; approve tolerable warnings, fix the rest and repeat
tools.notes: If only approved messages remain, the dialog does not open and the status bar shows e.g. 'ERC: 2 approved errors/warnings'. Run ERC often while drawing, and again after library updates or REPLACE.

tools.name: ERC messages
tools.description: Typical ERC findings documented in the release notes: nets with only one pin ('Only one pin on net'), output pins mixed with other drivers on a net ('OUTPUT and ... pins mixed on net', naming the pin direction), supply pins without a net, nets without pins, close but unconnected wires, net segments without a visible connection (label, bus or supply pin) to other segments of the same net, and pins connected without a visible wire, junction or pin. Further checks cover parts with user-definable values that have none, unconnected input pins of uninvoked gates, net names missing from the bus they connect to, nets or busses overlapping ports, incompatible HIZ pins and MUST gates that were not invoked.
tools.usage: ERC; then ERRORS
tools.example: Warning 'Segment of net VBUS has no visual connection (like Label, Bus or Supply pin) to other segments of the same net' -> add a LABEL to each segment or a supply symbol.
tools.notes: The pin Direction (NC, In, Out, IO, OC, Hiz, Pas, Pwr, Sup) defined in the library drives most of these checks.

tools.name: Consistency errors
tools.description: ERC findings that describe differences between the loaded schematic and board (missing or extra parts, differing names, values, packages, nets/signals or attributes). While any exist, forward & back annotation stays off, and they can never be approved - they must be fixed with NAME, VALUE, REPLACE, PINSWAP, ATTRIBUTE or CHANGE PACKAGE and confirmed by another ERC.
tools.usage: ERC with both files loaded > ERRORS > Consistency errors
tools.example: The ERC lists R12 under Consistency errors because its value differs between board and schematic -> set the correct value (VALUE R12 4k7) and run ERC; again until 'Board and schematic are consistent' is reported.
tools.notes: Differences between part and element attributes are treated as consistency errors. The eaglerc switch Erc.AllowUserOverrideConsistencyCheck enables forcing annotation anyway, at your own risk.

tools.name: Pin direction and the ERC
tools.description: Each symbol pin has a Direction that the ERC uses to judge connections and that controls automatic power wiring: NC (not connected), In, Out (totem-pole), IO (bidirectional, default), OC (open collector/drain), Hiz (3-state), Pas (passive), Pwr (power input) and Sup (supply symbol pin). Pwr pins are connected automatically to the net of a Sup pin with the same name.
tools.usage: Library symbol editor: CHANGE DIRECTION IN | OUT | IO | OC | HIZ | PAS | PWR | SUP | NC, then click the pin
tools.example: CHANGE DIRECTION PWR   # click the VCC and GND pins of a logic gate symbol so they connect to supply nets implicitly
tools.notes: In the XML format the direction is the pin attribute direction="nc|in|out|io|oc|pwr|pas|hiz|sup".

tools.name: UL_ERROR
tools.description: User Language object that exposes ERC and DRC results to ULPs through the errors() loop of UL_BOARD and UL_SCHEMATIC. It provides code, description, state (ERROR_STATE_ACTIVE, _APPROVED, _PROCESSED), type (ERROR_TYPE_WARNING, _ERROR, _CONSISTENCY), signature, area and position; in boards also the layer and the error polygon's contours(), in schematics the sheet, modulename, a second area in the board and strings s1..s6 with details such as names.
tools.usage: board(B) { if (B.checked) B.errors(ER) { ... } }   |   schematic(S) { if (S.checked) S.errors(ER) { ... } }
tools.notes: checked tells whether a DRC/ERC has been run on the loaded drawing; without it the list is empty.

tools.name: export-error.ulp
tools.description: Shipped ULP that exports or saves the DRC or ERC errors of the current board or schematic, running the check first if necessary. It is a practical way to get the error list as a text file for reviews or automated checks.
tools.usage: RUN export-error [SAVE] [filename]   (its own usage text writes 'export-errors')
tools.example: RUN export-error SAVE D:/out/demo2_drc.txt

tools.name: Autorouter and design rules
tools.description: The integrated autorouter (AUTO command, also used as Follow-me router by ROUTE) routes within the design rules and net classes of the board. Its control parameters are stored in the board (<autorouter> passes) and in .ctl files loaded or saved with AUTO LOAD/SAVE, and each run writes a protocol file name.pro. Wires in the Dimension layer bound the routing area, and objects in tRestrict, bRestrict and vRestrict are restricted areas for top, bottom and vias.
tools.usage: AUTO   (dialog) | AUTO; | AUTO LOAD file.ctl; | AUTO SAVE file.ctl;
tools.notes: Whether the autorouter module is available depends on the license/edition. Verify the design rules before starting any automatic router (BGA fan-out, quick routes).

tools.name: Cross-reference labels
tools.description: A net label with the xref property shows, besides the net name, the next (orientation R0/R270) or previous (R90/R180) sheet on which the net appears, typically placed at the sheet border. Its text follows the 'Xref label format' with the placeholders %F (flag border), %N (net name), %S (sheet), %C (column) and %R (row), default "%F%N/%S.%C%R"; column and row need a frame on the target sheet, otherwise '?' is shown.
tools.usage: LABEL XREF [orientation] • •   |   CHANGE XREF ON | OFF   |   SET XREF_LABEL_FORMAT string;
tools.example:
SET XREF_LABEL_FORMAT '%F%N/%S.%C%R';
LABEL XREF R0 (180 100) (185 100);
tools.notes: Works for nets, not busses. The format is stored in the schematic (xreflabel attribute of <schematic>); a net present only on the current sheet shows just its name.

tools.name: Part cross-references (>XREF)
tools.description: For relays and similar parts whose coil and contacts are spread over several sheets, each contact symbol can show where the coil is. Give the coil gate the add level Must and place the text variable >XREF in the contact symbols; it is replaced by sheet, column and row according to the 'Xref part format' (%S, %C, %R, default "/%S.%C%R").
tools.usage: Symbol: TEXT '>XREF'   Device: ADD coil symbol with addlevel MUST   Format: SET XREF_PART_FORMAT string;
tools.example: SET XREF_PART_FORMAT '/%S.%C%R';   # contact K1B shows e.g. /2.C4 where coil K1A is drawn
tools.notes: The format is stored in the schematic's xrefpart attribute.

tools.name: Contact cross-references (>CONTACT_XREF)
tools.description: Shows below a relay coil all contact gates of the device with the sheets and frame positions where they are used. Contact symbols need >XREF, pins extending up and down and their origin at the centre; in the device the first contact gate sits at x = 0 with its lower pin in the positive area (e.g. y = 100 mil) and the others to its right at the same y. The drawing is placed at the coil's x-position below the y-coordinate of the >CONTACT_XREF text in the frame symbol or on the sheet.
tools.usage: Place TEXT '>CONTACT_XREF' in the frame symbol or on the sheet; prepare the device as described
tools.example: Frame symbol: TEXT '>CONTACT_XREF' (0 20);   # coil K1 on sheet 1 then shows its contacts rotated 90 degrees with /2.B3, /3.A1 ...
tools.notes: The contact cross-reference cannot be selected; it moves with the coil and is refreshed at the next window redraw after invoking, moving or swapping contact gates.

tools.name: default.dru
tools.description: The default design rules file, looked up in the first Design rules directory when a new board is created (a copy ships in examples\design rules\examples). It describes a general two-layer setup (1*16) with 6 mil clearances, widths and drill distance, 40 mil copper-to-dimension, 0.35 mm minimum drill, 25 % annular rings (min 10 mil pads, 8 mil vias), a fixed 4 mil stop-mask oversize and no cream reduction. Its plain 'key = value' text shows every .dru parameter.
tools.usage: DRC LOAD default.dru;   or copy it to your Design rules directory and edit
tools.example: description[en] = EAGLE Design Rules... layerSetup = (1*16) mdWireWire = 6mil mdCopperDimension = 40mil msWidth = 6mil msDrill = 0.35mm rvPadTop = 0.250000 rlMinViaOuter = 8mil mlMinStopFrame = 4mil checkFont = 1
tools.notes: It also contains keys not explained in the help (mnLayersViaInSmd, mdSmdStop) and legacy Supply keys; save your own variant under a new name and edit its description.

tools.name: Eurocircuits design rules
tools.description: Manufacturer rule files from Eurocircuits in examples\design rules\examples\Eurocircuits: eC_Defaults (1 to 8 layers, pattern class 6, their default service) and eC_Advanced (pattern classes 3 to 9 with various base-copper thicknesses). File names encode layer count, pattern class and outer/inner base copper, and PDFs explain the classification and settings.
tools.usage: DRC LOAD "C:/Program Files/EAGLE 9.6.0/examples/design rules/examples/Eurocircuits/eC_Defaults/eC_2Layer_PClass6_BaseCopperO18_eCDefault.dru";
tools.example:
eC_2Layer_PClass6_BaseCopperO18_eCDefault.dru: 0.15 mm width and clearance, 0.35 mm minimum drill, 0.25 mm copper-to-edge
eC_4Layer_PClass8_BaseCopperO12-I18.dru: setup (1+2*3+16), 0.1 mm width/clearance, 0.25 mm minimum drill
tools.notes: Lower minimum drills than set are possible but move the board into a higher drill class (see the files' descriptions).

tools.name: Multi-CB design rules
tools.description: Rule files from Multi-CB in three groups: Multi-CB_Standard (1 to 8 layers, 100 um tracks, 0.2 mm drills, about 35 um final copper, no surcharge), Multi-CB_HDI (2, 4 and 6 layers, 75 um tracks, micro vias down to 0.075 mm) and Multi-CB_Thick-Cu (200 or 250 um tracks for 70/105 um copper). Their descriptions note that vias up to 0.45 mm are covered with solder mask and that only vector fonts should be used.
tools.usage: DRC LOAD ".../examples/design rules/examples/Multi-CB/Multi-CB_Standard/Multi-CB_2L_100um-Tracks_OL35um.dru";
tools.example: Multi-CB_4L_075um-Tracks_OL30um-IL12um.dru: setup (1+2*15+16), msWidth 0.075mm, mdWireWire 0.085mm, msMicroVia 0.075mm

tools.name: WEdirekt design rules
tools.description: Rule files from WEdirekt: EAGLE_WEdirekt_100/125/150/192_check.dru for 100 to 192 um structures, and WEd_1-2-1 / WEd_1-4-1 files for HDI builds (board thickness 0.8, 1.0 or 1.6 mm, 100 or 125 um structures) that use blind vias. The HDI files state that they are meant for experienced users only.
tools.usage: DRC LOAD ".../examples/design rules/examples/WEdirekt/EAGLE_WEdirekt_150_check.dru";
tools.example:
EAGLE_WEdirekt_150_check.dru: setup (1*2+3*4+13*14+15*16), 0.15 mm width/clearance
WEd_1-4-1_100mm_100m_V100.dru: setup ([2:1+2*3+14*15+16:15]), 0.1 mm structures, 0.15 mm micro vias
